subject.title: [Feature]: Track data provenance across session boundaries for persistent state

question: Should OpenClaw add a core/plugin-API provenance chain for durable state writes and future reads, and what provenance metadata may be persisted and exposed to plugins?
rationale: The remaining work defines security boundaries, public plugin contracts, persistent schema, migration behavior, and read-time trust policy, so automation cannot choose the API shape safely.

options.title: Design Minimal Provenance Contract First
options.body: Specify the metadata model, plugin visibility rules, migration or unknown-provenance behavior, and read-time policy hook before implementation.

options.title: Split Hook Prerequisites First
options.body: Land narrower before_tool_call and before_persistence_write API decisions first, then return to durable provenance once those contracts settle.

options.title: Defer To Plugins For Now
options.body: Close the direction only if maintainers decide current memory/plugin surfaces are enough and no missing core API should be added yet.

recommendation.title: Design Minimal Provenance Contract First
recommendation.body: Specify the metadata model, plugin visibility rules, migration or unknown-provenance behavior, and read-time policy hook before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete introduced the adjacent inter-session provenance contract and is the strongest history-backed owner for the cross-session security boundary decision.
